newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel eases closure of West Bank and Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Israel eases closure of West Bank and Gaza.

text.p: Thousands of Palestinians reached jobs in Israel on Sunday after the Jewish state eased a closure it imposed on the West Bank and Gaza in response to an Islamist bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe last month.

"Twenty thousand workers from the West Bank and Gaza Strip who are 35 years and older, married and hold security permits were allowed to enter to work in Israel as of Sunday," an Israeli army spokesman said.
Palestinian labour officials said only about half that number of workers met the criteria to enter Israel on Sunday.

The army sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip on March 21 after a Hamas militant killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe and died himself when the bomb he intended to plant there exploded prematurely.

The Tel Aviv attack came three days after Israel broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, sparking widespread Arab anger and a wave of Palestinian unrest in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Said Mudallal of the Palestinian Authority Labour Ministry said that Israel, by raising the minimum age of workers allowed work permits from 28 to 35, limited the eligibility of many unemployed Palestinians to find work in the Jewish state.

"With the new Israeli conditions and taking into consideration that the entry permits of around 60 percent of all workers expired during the closure, only 5,000 workers entered Israel from the Gaza Strip and around the same number from the West Bank," Mudallal told Reuters.

Israel has periodically sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip for security reasons since parts of the territories fell under Palestinian self-rule in 1994 under a Israeli-PLO peace deal. More than 60,000 Palestinians held jobs in Israel before 1994.
